subject: DPA addendum request: PII scoping, KMS and subprocessor map
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acmehealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: DPA addendum request: PII scoping, KMS and subprocessor map

Hi Marcus / Neha,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. As we move toward executing a DPA addendum with Acme Health, our security team has a few clarifying questions related to how Redwood handles PII for regulated workloads.

High level ask:
- Can you provide an updated dataflow diagram showing where customer PII is stored, processed, and cached (including KV cache and any transient storage)?
- Clarify KMS key custody: do you support customer-managed keys (BYOK) and can you attest that keys are never exportable from your HSM?
- Subprocessors: we need the current list of subprocessors that can access plaintext PII, and the contractual controls in place.

Attachments: Acme_Security_Questionnaire_v2.pdf (pdf)

Ideal timeline: can you provide these artifacts and a short response by EOD Friday (2026-05-14)?

Thanks,
Lena Ortiz
Security Manager, Acme Health
Attachments: Acme_Security_Questionnaire_v2.pdf (pdf)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-12T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA addendum request: PII scoping, KMS and subprocessor map

Hi Lena — thanks for the clear list. I'll coordinate responses. Quick summary of what we can deliver this week:
- High-level dataflow diagram annotated for PII handling (we'll include KV cache, retentions, and cross-region flow).
- BYOK support: yes for Redwood Private and Dedicated; for Hosted API we offer customer-managed keys in supported regions — will include attestation language.
- Subprocessor list with roles and access level; we'll call out any subprocessors with potential admin access to ciphertext/keys.

Looping in Neha and Evelyn to fill in the legal/technical details and attachments.

Next steps: I'll share updated diagram and a short answers doc by EOD Friday.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
Attachments: initial_dataflow_sketch.png (png)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acmehealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-13T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA addendum request: PII scoping, KMS and subprocessor map

Lena, Marcus — thanks. A few clarifications from legal before we hand off technical artifacts:

Please confirm:
1) Which Acme workload(s) are in scope (product names / environment: prod/stage)? We need this to tie to contract exhibits.
2) If you require BYOK for Hosted API, confirm whether Acme will provide an HSM provider (AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault / GCP CMEK) or needs Redwood to broker.
3) Evidence list: SOC 2 report (latest), KMS key custody diagram, subprocessor contracts/redlines (if any).

We can provide redacted SOC 2 and a notarized key custody attestation. For subprocessors, we'll provide role-level exposure (admin vs maintenance) and whether they can decrypt PII.

I'll have the legal addendum draft ready for your review by Tuesday 2026-05-19.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Security
Attachments: legal_addendum_template.docx (docx)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acmehealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-14T14:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA addendum request: PII scoping, KMS and subprocessor map

Hi Lena — attaching the annotated dataflow and an access matrix export.

Summary:
- Dataflow highlights: PII ingested via API endpoints -> tokenization layer (optional) -> model serving runtime. KV cache holds recent session state; TTL configurable per-customer (default 1h). Persistent stores: audit logs (hashed identifiers), model input retention (configurable 30/90/365 days). Cross-region replication only occurs for Dedicated deployments when enabled.
- KMS: BYOK supported for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted, CMEK available in select regions (we'll list them). Keys are stored in FIPS 140-2 HSMs and are non-exportable. We include a signed attestation PDF in the attachments.
- Subprocessors: only a small set (monitoring vendor, infra provider, paid support partner). We mark which can access plaintext in emergency support scenarios; otherwise plaintext never leaves customer tenant without explicit consent.

Attachments: pii_dataflow_v3.png (png), access_matrix_export.csv (csv), kms_attestation_signed.pdf (pdf)

Let me know if you want a short walkthrough call; we can book 30 mins.

—Evelyn Hart
Product Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acmehealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-15T08:55:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA addendum request: PII scoping, KMS and subprocessor map

Thanks — these are helpful. A couple follow-ups before we close:
- Can you confirm whether tokenization is performed client-side or server-side for Hosted API?
- We need a short attestation for "no export of customer keys" suitable for our procurement team (a single-page letter).
- Can you confirm retention defaults for model inputs for prod workloads (we are leaning toward 30 days)?

If you can provide the attestation and confirm tokenization flow by EOD Monday (2026-05-17) we'll schedule the contract signature.

Marcus — suggested plan: 5/17 attestation + tokenization note; 5/19 legal review; 5/21 final addendum and DocuSign.

Thanks,
Lena

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-15T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA addendum request: PII scoping, KMS and subprocessor map

Lena — noted. We'll deliver:
- 1-page KMS non-export attestation (signed) by 2026-05-17 EOD.
- Confirmation: tokenization is server-side for Hosted API unless customer opts into a client-side tokenization SDK (we'll include SDK docs).
- Retention default: 30 days for model inputs in production (configurable per contract).

I'll attach the attestation and tokenization note in a follow-up email today.

Marcus Lin
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
Attachments: kms_nonexport_attestation_signed.pdf (pdf), tokenization_design_note.pdf (pdf)
